label: GPT-6.1 Terra
output:
**One star for now: good interface, but we need support that responds**

We signed a three-year contract with Stackhouse Cloud in June 2026 for $14,200 a year and went live on October 19. We’re a one-branch community library with two full-time staff, volunteers, and about 2,300 active cardholders. We don’t have an IT department to fall back on when something goes wrong.

Since October 28, checkouts have worked only offline on one laptop, and our holds queue has been wiped out—around 640 holds. A retired rancher drove 40 minutes to pick up his held large-print Westerns. We had no record of the hold and had to send him home with nothing. One of our volunteers has been writing checkouts on index cards like it’s 1975.

Our support ticket has been open for 12 days. We’ve received three replies, each saying the issue has been escalated to engineering. Our sales rep promised a “dedicated migration specialist.” What we got was a shared inbox.

To be fair, the software looked good in the demo, and the staff interface is better than our old system. My concern is not the product idea. It’s whether a small library can get meaningful help when circulation stops working and patron records are affected.

I’m asking someone senior at Stackhouse to assign a named person to call me this week, explain the recovery plan, and give us a realistic timeline. Our county budget hearing is November 18, and this line item is on the agenda. I need to be able to explain where things stand.

For other library directors considering Stackhouse: ask for support response times in writing before you sign, and ask who will actually be responsible for your migration.

One star for now. I’ll revisit this review if Stackhouse fixes the problems and we can rely on the service.
